name: LegalZoom.com, Inc.

profile.description: LegalZoom.com, Inc. is an online platform providing legal, compliance and tax solutions primarily to small businesses and consumers in the United States, including business formation, registered agent and compliance subscriptions, estate-planning documents and access to independent attorneys. Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Glendale, California, it generated $756M of revenue in FY2025. Jeff Stibel, a ~5% holder and board chair, became CEO in July 2024.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): LegalZoom is shifting from one-time transactions to a 'subscription-led AI-enabled platform' [4]; Q2 2026 subscription revenue grew 11% to $133.4M while transaction revenue fell 1% to $71.9M [1] — a real but incremental mix shift of an existing model. AI Deployment (1/2): Management says AI has improved efficiency across legal services, sales and customer care [4], but no savings or AI revenue are quantified. Market Share (1/2): A long-standing leader in online business formation, but management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $795–805M from $810–830M citing the shift of customer discovery away from traditional search [1] — evidence it is not gaining share. Pipeline (0/2): No named next-generation products with launch dates or revenue targets were found. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D of $81.9M is 10.8% of FY2025 revenue [5], below typical application-software peers.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): LegalZoom's purpose of democratizing access to law for small businesses and families is specific and has been defended through two decades of unauthorized-practice-of-law fights with state bars in North Carolina, Missouri, South Carolina, Arkansas and New Jersey [7]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive foundation or quantified community program was found. Employee Retention (0/2): The company announced a 13% workforce reduction alongside its August 2026 guidance cut [1], and leadership changed in July 2024 when Stibel replaced Dan Wernikoff [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): Stibel holds ~5% [6], but no net open-market insider buying in the trailing 12 months was found.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically on 7 metrics (Growth sleeve, 10 weight units). D/E 11.9% (1.00) and forward P/E 8.3 (1.00) are excellent [8]; ROE 10.5% (0.70, 2x), YoY revenue growth 6.6% (0.89), and 5-yr revenue CAGR 9.9% from $470.6M (FY2020) to $756.0M (FY2025) (1.00, 2x) [5][8]. GAAP profit margin is thin at 2.1% (0.11), and FMP's forward PEG of 5.0 (0.00, 2x) reflects minimal GAAP EPS growth [9]. Weighted sum 6.38/10 → 6. Liquidity: ~2.87M shares/day × $6.72 ≈ $19.3M/day, above the floor. Free cash flow of ~$125M against $167M cash and $15M debt shows the cash generation GAAP earnings understate [8].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (3/9): LegalZoom sells standardized legal documents and filings acquired largely through search — the exact workflow that generative AI assistants are absorbing. Management cut 2026 guidance citing the 'industry-wide shift in customer discovery away from traditional search' and Google search changes [1], and conceded traffic from AI sources 'remains limited' [4]; registered-agent and compliance subscriptions and state filing mechanics provide only partial protection. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is described as an efficiency tool and part of an 'AI-enabled platform' [4], but no AI revenue is quantified.

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would credit LegalZoom's founding cause — making law accessible to people who cannot afford a lawyer — and its willingness to fight state bars for two decades to keep that door open [7]. But the current company is managing a finite problem: guidance cut twice in 2026, a 13% layoff, and a CEO change in 2024 [1][6]. The organization is reacting to channel disruption rather than leading a reinvention.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Democratizing legal help for small businesses and families is distinctive and service-oriented, and it has been tested through UPL litigation since the 2000s [7]. It has not, however, become the organizing advantage in the AI era — strategy today is framed in subscription mix and EBITDA margin [1].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The company repeatedly took on state bars and class actions rather than retreat from its model, including suing the North Carolina State Bar [7]. Stibel's move from chair to CEO as a ~5% owner signals personal commitment [6], but the 2026 response — guidance cuts and layoffs [1] — is defensive rather than a costly long-term bet.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A 13% workforce reduction in August 2026 [1] follows the abrupt 2024 CEO transition [6]; no evidence of high trust, long tenure or low turnover was found.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The pivot from transactional document sales to recurring compliance subscriptions (now growing 11% while transactions shrink) [1] is a genuine adaptation, and management is repositioning as an AI-enabled platform [4], but the outcome is unproven.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found acknowledging competitors' strengths or framing AI-native rivals as a source of learning; competition is discussed as channel pressure on customer acquisition [1].

investment_thesis: LegalZoom is cheap on cash flow: ~$125M of free cash flow on a ~$1.15B market cap, $167M of cash against $15M of debt, and a forward P/E of 8.3 [8]. Subscriptions — now about two-thirds of revenue — grew 11% in Q2 2026 to $133.4M, and adjusted EBITDA guidance of $190–195M implies 12% growth and a 24% margin despite lower revenue guidance [1]. A ~5% owner-CEO has an incentive to drive per-share value [6].
thesis_continued: The core risk is that generative AI is dismantling LegalZoom's customer-acquisition engine and commoditizing its documents. FY2026 revenue guidance has fallen from $805–825M to $795–805M, Q3 guidance implies just 2% growth, and transaction revenue is shrinking [1]. GAAP margins are only 2.1% and FMP's forward PEG is 5.0 [8][9]. The 13% layoff signals cost defense rather than offense, and recurring UPL litigation remains a background legal risk [7].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results versus $192–196M revenue guidance (2% growth at midpoint) and evidence that subscription growth (+11% in Q2) is holding [1]
Delivery of the $190–195M adjusted EBITDA outlook after the 13% workforce reduction [1]
Growth in traffic referred by AI assistants, which management called limited but expected to grow [4]
Capital return funded by ~$125M annual free cash flow and a net-cash balance sheet [8]
key_risks: Customer discovery shifting from Google search to AI assistants, already cited for the 2026 guidance cut [1]
Commoditization of LLC formation and estate documents as AI tools generate them free or at low cost
Transaction revenue declining (-1% in Q2 2026) faster than subscriptions can offset [1]
Ongoing unauthorized-practice-of-law litigation, including the 2024 New Jersey class action sent to arbitration in 2025 [7]
